S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation, is characterized by persistent hyperactivity and impulsivity that are developmentally inappropriate, present across settings, and associated with functional impairment. In adults and older adults it may appear less as overt running or climbing and more as marked inner restlessness, excessive activity, difficulty engaging quietly, interrupting, blurting, and trouble waiting. It is distinguished from episodic mood states or situational agitation by its chronic course and cross-situational pattern rather than discrete episodes.

patient.stressor_event: Changing to a different line of work
patient.stressor: Jorge Rosado’s move from familiar student jobs and art-focused routines into radiologic technology training placed him in a much more regulated clinical environment where timing, turn-taking, and waiting for complete instructions mattered for patient flow and safety. Across the next 1 year and 5 months, the high-energy style that had once fueled sketching, photography, and pickup basketball became clinically consequential as he struggled to remain still during required downtime, talked or moved through quiet clinical spaces, answered supervisors before they finished, and had repeated difficulty waiting his turn during imaging procedures and lab practice. The pattern affected evaluations, patient communication, and teamwork to the point that his program placed him on a formal remediation plan. Jorge sought psychiatric care through student health after realizing that effort, checklists, and fitness routines were not enough to keep the problem from threatening his training.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: I came in because I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still in the radiology suite or classroom, and after months of trying to tough it out I still end up pacing, shifting, or finding some excuse to move.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even when I’m doing something I like, like editing photos or sketching, I can’t keep it quiet for long—I start tapping, humming, talking to whoever’s nearby, or getting up so much that people in the lab or at home tell me to settle down.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: Most days I go from class to clinicals to the gym to errands without really stopping, and if there’s a gap in the schedule I immediately fill it with something because sitting around feels almost impossible.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: When a supervisor is explaining a positioning step or asking me a question, I’ll jump in with the answer before they finish, and then I realize I missed the part that actually mattered.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Waiting my turn during lab practice or for a machine to open up makes me so edgy that I keep stepping forward, checking the time, and asking if I can go next, which has gotten me called out more than once.

add_requirements.Onset prior to age 12 years: My parents still talk about elementary school conferences where teachers said I was always out of my seat, calling out, or rushing ahead before directions were finished. That was happening way before middle school, not just since radiology training.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My clinical evaluations have taken a hit, and I was put on a formal remediation plan because supervisors say my behavior disrupts patient flow and makes teamwork harder. I’m worried it could cost me my place in the program if I don’t get it under control.
add_requirements.duration: This has been causing serious problems since I switched into radiologic technology training about 1 year and 5 months ago.
